To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed four mAb specific for LMP and TAp subunits that will be valuable reagants to analyze the cellular and tissue distribution of these molecules in normal and transformed human cells.
the mAb immunoreacted with the corresponding Lmp2, Lmp7, TAP 1 and TAP 2 subunits and stained keratinocytes as well as lymphocytes in frozen as well as paraffin embedded skin sections.
we have developed mAb to human LMP2, TAP1, TAP2 and LMP2 that can be used to analyze their cellular expression in normal and transformed tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of monoclonal antibodies to human LMP2, 7, TAP-1, TAP-2, which will be useful tools for the analysis of the cellular distribution and tissue distribution of these proteins.
the generation of mAb to LMP2, 7, TAP 1 and TAP 2 and the characterization of these reagents.
the development of mAb against the LMP and TAPI and TAP2 subunits of the proteasome-transporter complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mAb described here are specific, and can be used to analyze the expression of LMP2, TAP1, LMP7 and TAP2 in normal and transformed human cells.

the mAb we generated in this study are specific for the respective antigens and that they will be useful reagents for the analysis of LMP and the TAP subunits, in particular for the study of their cellular expression, structure and tissue distribution.
the mAbs described herein are specific for the LMP and TAPI and TAP2 proteins and that they can be used for the detection of these proteins in human tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have generated a panel of mAb against LMP2, -7, TAP-1, -2, and that these antibodies are suitable for immunohistochemistry, immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence.
we have generated and characterized four new mouse mAb, specific to LMP2, TAP1, LMP7 and TAP2, respectively.

the anti-LMP mAb are suitable to detect LMP2 and Lmp7 in immunohistochemistry and the anti-TAP mab can be used to detect TAP1 and/or TAP2 in Western blotting, immunoprecipitation and immunohistochemistry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mAb can be used for the detection of the corresponding LMPs or TAP subunits in immunohistochemical and immunoprecipitation studies.

it is possible to generate mAb to LMP2, 7, TAP 1 and TAP 2 from immunization with the corresponding proteins or peptides, and that the reactivity of these mAb is consistent with the expression pattern of the proteins in human cells.
it will be possible to use these antibodies to study the role of these molecules in normal and transformed human cells, and to develop new diagnostic tools.
